goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts:3 — All import() calls fire eagerly at module load, so a failure in any single app package yields a rejected promise that is unhandled unless that exact key is later awaited, and nothing is actually lazy-loaded.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the object literal assigns each key to the result of calling `import("./...")` (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`). Those `import()` expressions execute immediately when the module is evaluated, so all apps begin importing eagerly at module load time (not lazily on first access). If any of those dynamic imports rejects and that specific promise is never awaited/caught (because that integration is never used), it can produce an unhandled rejection; even if awaited later, it may still be considered unhandled until a handler is attached. The diff also shows consumers changed to `await appStore[...]`, but only for the keys they use, leaving unused keys' import promises potentially unobserved.
